annote: SUPPORTS: the lineage of a simple time/state logistic in-game win-probability model for League of Legends, and of evaluating events by the change in a frozen estimated win probability. The paper fits on elapsed minutes and both teams’ cumulative kills, towers and large monsters, sampling one random minute per game for that step. DOES NOT SUPPORT: our feature schema, patch/cohort population, engagement definition, endpoint rule, V, q, calibration results, or any causal reading. Delta V remains a model-derived probability difference over our own window, not a counterfactual.

annote: SUPPORTS: inspecting an inter-activity-time distribution and separating within- from between-session components to derive an activity boundary. The paper fits an EM Gaussian mixture on log times and takes the likelihood intersection, offering about one hour as a rule of thumb while showing fitted intersections range from roughly 29 to 115 minutes across logs. DOES NOT SUPPORT: G = 13.7 s, which is this project’s pooled KDE-valley estimate on kill gaps; a KDE valley and a mixture intersection are different estimators on different populations. It justifies neither our engagement window nor any causal claim.

annote: SUPPORTS: additive feature attribution as a unified framework, with attributions defined relative to an explanation mapping and summing to the represented model output under stated assumptions, and with feature dependence and background data affecting interpretation. DOES NOT SUPPORT: causal explanation. Our seven-group exact Shapley computation with fixed p_pre as one group, a 128-row background and 256 explained rows per cell explains the fitted, calibrated q output under those choices; it does not explain V or Delta V and does not show that a feature caused a teamfight to go well.
